description:
I am an Associate Professor in Computer Science and Engineering with a Ph.D. and passionate about developing innovative technology solutions to address real-world challenges. Our project aims to develop AI-powered Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions, focusing on real-time vital sign monitoring, health-risk prediction, anomaly detection, and intelligent alerts to support astronaut well-being.

I welcome enthusiastic team members with skills in Python, AI/ML.
summary: SPACECARE AI is a web-based astronaut health monitoring platform developed using React and Firebase to support astronauts in assessing and managing their health during space missions. The application enables astronauts to securely log in using individual astronaut IDs, record health indicators such as blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep duration, mood, nutrition and urine color for hydration assessment, and maintain historical health records. It integrates health analytics, AI-assisted risk assessment, personalized health recommendations and an emergency alert system with automatic health-risk detection and manual SOS activation. The platform provides an intuitive medical dashboard to visualize health conditions and identify potential warning signs. By enabling continuous self-assessment, early identification of health concerns and timely medical intervention, SPACECARE AI addresses the challenges of limited access to immediate medical assistance during space missions and supports astronaut health, safety and mission sustainability.
details:
1. What does the project do and how does it work?

SPACECARE AI is a web-based health monitoring and self-assessment platform designed to help astronauts monitor their physical and psychological well-being during space missions. Astronauts log in using their individual astronaut IDs and manually enter health indicators, including blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, body temperature, daily sleep hours, mood, nutritional information and urine color as a hydration indicator. The application stores assessment records securely in Firebase Firestore, enabling astronauts to review their health history. It incorporates health analytics, AI-assisted health risk assessment, personalized health recommendations and an emergency alert system that identifies predefined warning conditions and supports manual SOS activation.

2. What are the benefits?

  • Enables astronauts to perform regular self-health assessments without depending entirely on immediate medical assistance.
  • Supports early identification of potential health concerns.
  • Monitors hydration through an interactive eight-color urine assessment indicator.
  • Maintains individual astronaut health records and assessment history.
  • Provides personalized health improvement and wellness recommendations.
  • Supports emergency identification through automatic alerts and manual SOS activation.

3. What is the intended impact?

The primary objective is to improve astronaut health monitoring, promote preventive healthcare and support timely medical intervention during space missions. By integrating multiple health indicators into a unified platform, SPACECARE AI aims to help astronauts recognize potential health risks, make informed health-related decisions and maintain their physical and psychological well-being. The solution can contribute to safer, healthier and more sustainable long-duration space missions.

4. What tools, programming languages and software were used?

The project was developed using the following technologies:

  • Frontend: React.js, JavaScript, HTML5 and CSS3.
  • Backend and Database: Firebase and Cloud Firestore.
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio Code on Windows.
  • UI Components: Lucide React icons and responsive CSS-based dashboard components.
  • Data Management: Firebase Authentication and Firestore for astronaut identification, health assessment storage and historical records.
  • Health Analytics: Rule-based health indicator evaluation and AI-assisted assessment and recommendation modules.

The current prototype uses manual health data entry. Wearable-device integration is considered a possible future enhancement.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

SPACECARE AI combines physical health monitoring, psychological well-being assessment, nutrition, hydration monitoring and emergency response within a single astronaut-focused application. One distinctive feature is its interactive eight-color urine indicator, which provides an additional visual approach to hydration assessment. Instead of presenting isolated health measurements, the platform integrates multiple indicators to generate meaningful health insights and personalized recommendations. Its combination of self-assessment, historical tracking and emergency alert management makes it a comprehensive health support concept for space missions.

6. What factors did the team consider?

The development considered the unique challenges of the space environment, including microgravity-related physiological changes, immune system alterations, bone density loss, cardiovascular risks, nutritional deficiencies, sleep disturbances and behavioral health challenges. Other important considerations included ease of use, astronaut-specific authentication, secure health data storage, assessment history, understandable health visualizations, timely identification of warning signs and the limitations of accessing immediate medical assistance during missions.

SPACECARE AI is designed as a scalable prototype that can be further enhanced with advanced AI models, wearable-device connectivity, medical officer dashboards and mission-compatible emergency communication systems.
